newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. envoy urges Mexico to pursue privatisation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy urges Mexico to pursue privatisation.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to Mexico James Jones on Tuesday urged Mexico to go ahead with the privatisation of its petrochemical plants that have been held up by political difficulties.

"There are many other Latin American countries...who are privatising their energy and chemical operations and foreign investors are going there," Jones told reporters in a warning broadcast on Mexican television.
He acknowledged that the privatisations have been difficult for Mexico, but said "the government should resolve this matter to attract investments".

Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) sought at the weekend to block the sale of the petrochemical plants, which has already faced stiff opposition from leftist opposition parties and unions who see it as a threat to the sovereignty Mexico jealously guards over state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos.
Energy Ministry officials say they are studying the PRI's objections but insist the sales will go ahead.

National and international companies, including Terra and Farmland of the United States, have already placed bids for the first item on the block, a complex of ammonia plants in Cosoleacaque with annual sales of more than $400 million. The winner of that auction should have been named in April.
